item.title: BCCI’s big plan for Sooryavanshi: ‘Serve like Sachin, not be a one-year wonder’
item.description: The BCCI is diligently tracking 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's development in cricket. With his remarkable debut as India's youngest men's international player following an explosive IPL performance, the board aims to capitalise on his promise for a sustainable international career. They are keen to ensure he avoids being labeled a fleeting talent while closely mentoring a broader pool of young players at the Centre of Excellence.

item.title: Bezos got a special invite to ‘US exclusive Country Club’ but won’t get membership
item.description: Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez attended an exclusive club event as guests. Six months later, Bezos still awaits membership despite owning island properties. Membership at Indian Creek Country Club requires more than significant financial investment. Other prominent residents also face challenges in securing club membership. The club's stringent approval process emphasizes member relationships and committee decisions.

item.title: Michael Jordan demolishes $2.8M Lake Norman mansion for new estate
item.description: Michael Jordan’s $2.8 million Lake Norman property is undergoing a major transformation. Purchased in 2013, the site’s original six-bedroom, eight-bathroom mansion was demolished in March 2025. New aerial pictures now show the NBA legend’s custom luxury estate taking shape inside the exclusive Peninsula Club, with its structure and roofing apparently nearing completion.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: Apple and Google rename Lake Ontario to Lake America; one app refuses Trump’s order
item.description: MapQuest's refusal to comply with a federal directive to rename Lake Ontario has landed the app at the peak of the US App Store charts. Unlike Google Maps and Apple Maps, which followed the presidential order, MapQuest experienced a remarkable boost, collecting over 1.5 million downloads in North America. The company is now shifting focus towards new features that users are eager for.

item.title: Travis Kelce’s $1.5M charity under scrutiny: Why did less go to charity?
item.description: Travis Kelce’s Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation is facing scrutiny over its reported spending between 2021 and 2024. The nonprofit raised $1.5 million and spent about $1.1 million, with $469,000 listed for management and $446,000 for charity. Kelce’s business manager Aaron Eanes disputed the figures, saying some charitable operational costs were misclassified. He said management fees dropped to zero in 2025 as the foundation works to improve transparency and governance.

item.title: Paswan vs Manjhi: SC 'creamy layer' debate divides NDA; will it open Pandora's box?
item.description: Two influential Dalit leaders in Bihar are embroiled in a public discourse about sub-quotas related to existing reservations. This rift within the Scheduled Caste community may stir up political complexities for the NDA government. The BJP must navigate the demands of anti-reservation activists and also its allies, who seek changes in reservation policy, even as it strives to maintain the balance of its electoral coalition pressures.
item.dc:creator: KUNAL VARMA

item.title: Asia Cup: India storm into semis as Mandhana’s record 124, spin blitz crush Hong Kong
item.description: In a stunning display of skill, Smriti Mandhana smashed 124 runs, leading India to an impressive total. The bowlers followed suit, limiting Hong Kong to just 56 runs. This commanding 137-run victory not only showcased India's strength but also secured their entry into the Women's Asia Cup semi-finals, with Mandhana setting new records in women's international cricket.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.title: 8th pay commission: How level 8 staff could earn up to Rs 28.89 lakh extra in 10 yrs
item.description: Employee bodies have argued that the current 3% annual increment is not sufficient to keep pace with rising expenses. Their recommendations have ranged from 5% to 7%. If such proposals are accepted, a higher increment rate of 5% or 7% would have a direct impact on the salary progression of central government employees.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: Smriti Mandhana equals Mithali Raj’s big record, then creates more history
item.description: Smriti Mandhana achieved a significant milestone by equaling Mithali Raj's record for fifty-plus scores. She reached this landmark during India's Women's Asia Cup match against Hong Kong China. Mandhana then transitioned to an exceptional T20I century, scoring 124 runs off 64 balls. This remarkable innings also set a new record for the highest individual score in the Women's T20 Asia Cup.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: Nepal floods: No bodies to cremate, kin burn kusha effigies as hopes fade for missing
item.description: Families in Nuwakot and Rasuwa performed symbolic cremations for missing flood victims. Relatives used kusha grass effigies when bodies could not be recovered. Searches for missing kin proved unsuccessful across various locations. Priests guided families through traditional rituals for liberating souls. Over one hundred effigies were cremated in Kathmandu's Pashupati Aryaghat.
item.dc:creator: VISHANT AGARWALA

item.title: Smriti Mandhana creates history, surpasses Lanning to become leading century-maker
item.description: In an exhilarating display of skill, Smriti Mandhana shattered records by scoring her 18th international century, amassing 124 runs in just 64 balls. Her explosive knock led India to a formidable total of 193 runs. Shafali Verma played a vital role at the start with her brisk 28, setting the tone for a dominant batting showcase by the Indian team.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.title: After mother's death, Wyoming rancher vowed to protect 2,506 acres forever
item.description: David Ellsbury honored his late mother's wish by safeguarding the family's cherished Diamond E Ranch from development. Spanning 2,506 acres, this land is now forever shielded by a land trust, ensuring that future generations can enjoy its unspoiled beauty. The ranching traditions of the family will thrive on this preserved estate.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: BCCI meeting decoded: Saikia reveals plans for injuries, SENA tours & 2027 WC
item.description: The BCCI is set to enhance its overseas performance strategy while tackling player injuries. They aim to craft a robust plan in preparation for the 2027 ODI World Cup, which will require adjustments in the Future Tours Programme to prioritise player rest. Recent defeats in white-ball matches against England and Ireland were carefully analysed, and insight was gathered from captains and the head coach regarding fitness protocols.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: 7.8% growth, but a Rs 6 lakh crore question: Why GDP data has sparked a debate
item.description: One of the biggest points of discussion and questioning is the revision to Q1 FY26 GDP at current prices, that is the figures for last year's same quarter numbers. Under the old 2011-12 series, GDP was estimated at Rs 86.05 lakh crore. However, under the new series, it has subsequently been revised to Rs 80 lakh crore.
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: Why personal-guarantor recoveries are so tiny — and why Chandra’s was tinier still
item.description: Subhash Chandra was offering just 0.03% of the loans for which he was a personal guarantor. But there should be no surprise here. In the history of such settlements in India, guarantors have paid an average 1% of the amount they stood guarantee for
item.dc:creator: CHANDRIMA BANERJEE

item.title: KPSC irregularities: K'taka govt suspends IAS officer facing probe
item.description: Karnataka government suspended IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar due to KPSC recruitment irregularities. He is currently in CID custody as the agency investigates the commission's alleged wrongdoings. The Directorate of Enforcement is also conducting a separate investigation into the matter. Gangwar served as Controller of Examinations at KPSC during the period under scrutiny. His suspension is effective immediately pending further investigation by the CID.
item.dc:creator: VRITI JAIN

item.title: Goa's new housing law opens the door to revenue-sharing projects; here's why
item.description: The Goa Assembly has passed a bill allowing the Goa Housing Board to implement projects. This new legislation enables joint ventures and revenue-sharing models for housing development. The amendment empowers the board to partner with eligible entities for scheme implementation. This move aims to leverage practical and financial advantages for efficient project execution. The state government will soon frame rules for these new development partnerships.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: BCCI breaks silence on Asian Games concerns, promises ‘best facilities’ for Team India
item.description: The BCCI has responded to worries surrounding the accommodation for Indian cricket teams during the Asian Games, with secretary Devajit Saikia assuring that there are no pressing concerns. The board is dedicated to delivering high-quality amenities for both players and staff. Under VVS Laxman’s leadership, the men's team will compete, while Amol Muzumdar coaches the women's team, as India seek to retain their titles.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: Why Agarkar was not present in BCCI's meeting? Devajit Saikia reveals the reason
item.description: BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia clarified the situation surrounding Ajit Agarkar's absence from a recent board meeting. He shared that Agarkar was traveling and encountered connectivity problems that prevented him from joining virtually. Saikia also brushed aside any rumors about adjustments to the senior men's selection committee. The meeting primarily reviewed past performances and strategized for the upcoming 2027 ODI World Cup without addressing the potential appointment of a cricket director.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.title: Jennifer Aniston's boyfriend Jim opens up on partial paralysis due to nerve damage
item.description: Jim Curtis shared his journey of overcoming spinal cord lesions and partial paralysis. He spoke about accepting struggles and finding personal power through self-love. Curtis also advised on navigating life crossroads without abandoning responsibilities. Jennifer Aniston attended the event celebrating his new book, 'The Book of Possibility'. The couple has become more open about their relationship since 2025.

item.title: Bank holiday on Janmashtami: Where are banks closed on Sept 4, 2026? Check list
item.description: Indian banks across various states will be closed on September 4 to observe Krishna Janmashtami. Customers should be aware that further closures will occur throughout the month for additional festivals and elections. It's essential to check local holiday schedules for branch services, although digital banking and ATMs will continue to function normally. Plan accordingly for any urgent in-person banking needs during these times.

item.title: Couple buys Rs 60L flat, husband taxed on Rs 34.81L stamp-duty gap; ITAT objects
item.description: Can the entire difference between a property’s actual purchase price and its stamp-duty value be added to the income of just one of its co-owners? A recent ruling by ITAT Mumbai has addressed this question in a case involving a husband and wife who jointly purchased a property.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: Punjabi singer Baljeet Singh found dead; police launch probe
item.description: Baljeet Singh, a popular Punjabi singer, was tragically found deceased at his home in Ludhiana, prompting a police investigation initiated by a disturbing odor. Upon arrival, officers discovered his lifeless body on the bed, accompanied by noticeable signs of blood. Disturbingly, Singh had been out of touch with his family for several days. This shocking discovery occurs shortly after the murder of another regional music artist, Ankit Balyan.
